headline: Bedrock removal rules advance to City Council after a five-aye vote; planning grant for housing or cultural plan recommended.
summary: Most of the talk centered on noise from bedrock blasting and jackhammers in residential areas. Staff also asked for direction on transferable development rights, which apply to large homes and taller commercial buildings. A public hearing on technical zoning fixes was set for November 24th.
decisions: Approved bedrock removal rule changes (LDR2601) and sent them to City Council, five ayes, not unanimous.
Approved setting a public hearing for November 24th on technical zoning amendments (LDR2612), unanimously.
Recommended that City Council approve a municipal planning grant to fund either a housing action plan or a cultural plan, unanimously.
Approved adding Marshall District civic spaces to the landscaping project charge, unanimously.
discussion: Bedrock removal rules: Members debated whether the rules could limit noise from blasting and jackhammers, and whether the rules would be clear enough for the board to use.

Transferable development rights: Discussion covered a possible 2,000 to 2,500 square foot threshold, whether smaller purchase increments would work, and whether living space or footprint should count.
Commercial height rights: Industrial developers said buying transferable rights for extra building height adds large costs, and members discussed whether that cost works against city goals.
Act 250 and rare species review: Staff said the Act 250 hearing must stay open to November 12th, and that talks with the Agency of Natural Resources may change the rare species wording.
